title: Fleet Recall / Overview
description: Fleet health, latency, reliability, dependency pressure and worker freshness. Follow the linked dashboards for diagnosis.

panels.title: Start here
panels.description: How to read this view

options.content:
**Request health → Dependencies → Workers → Kubernetes → Logs**

Rates describe long-running processes. Worker snapshots describe **one completed invocation**. Missing data stays unknown; an available metrics endpoint does not prove database readiness. The service-instance filter does not filter worker collectors.

panels.title: Service targets up
panels.description: Available Prometheus scrape targets; compare with configured targets.

panels.title: MCP calls / second
panels.description: Recall and remember only. Transport/protocol traffic is shown on Requests.

panels.title: MCP error fraction
panels.description: Backend errors, deadlines and cancellations divided by observed MCP traffic. Success-only traffic has a known zero numerator. No observed traffic stays unknown; refused/invalid are separate outcomes.

panels.title: MCP p95
panels.description: Weighted across selected calls, including unsuccessful outcomes.

panels.title: Terminal outcomes
panels.description: Do not count an invalid/refused request as a successful write. Cancelled/timed-out writes can have an unknown durable outcome.

panels.title: HTTP failures by surface
panels.description: HTTP demo, ingress and authenticated remote MCP outcomes, separated by surface. HTTP operations and MCP calls can be nested. They must not be added together as a request total.

panels.title: Database and embedding p95
panels.description: Independent operation boundaries; local_batch and embed may describe nested work.

panels.title: Worker snapshot age
panels.description: Age of the last completed snapshot, successful or failed. Missing collectors/snapshots are shown on Workers. Default alert budget is 15 minutes.

panels.title: Latest worker result
panels.description: Succeeded, failed, or explicitly unknown per deployment/collector. A down collector or absent terminal worker outcome is unknown. Historical samples repeat the latest published snapshot, not a count or duration of runs.

targets.expr: ((max by (deployment,instance) (fleet_recall_operations_total{job="fleet-worker-textfile",deployment=~"$deployment",component="process",operation="worker",outcome="error"} or (0 * fleet_recall_operations_total{job="fleet-worker-textfile",deployment=~"$deployment",component="process",operation="worker",outcome="success"}))) and on (deployment,instance) (max by (deployment,instance) (up{job="fleet-worker-textfile",deployment=~"$deployment"}) == 1)) or on (deployment,instance) (0 * max by (deployment,instance) (up{job="fleet-worker-textfile",deployment=~"$deployment"}) + 2)

panels.title: Live scrape availability
panels.description: 0 is down. A removed target disappears; discovery/inventory checks are needed to detect removed targets.

panels.title: Fleet alerts
panels.description: Application alert rules currently aggregate deployment labels away; this panel intentionally lists all Fleet firing alerts with job and instance for context.

panels.title: Core readiness
panels.description: One means the bounded database check is fresh and successful. Missing data stays unknown. Embedding failure alone does not remove lexical service readiness.

panels.title: Readiness check age
panels.description: Elapsed wall time since the last completed readiness check. Startup has no successful probe; inspect core readiness and scrape availability together.

panels.title: Remote HTTP responses
panels.description: HTTP classes across MCP, grants and shipping; tool failures inside HTTP 200 are tracked separately by the existing MCP panels. No path, scope or client identifier is retained.

panels.title: Remote HTTP denials
panels.description: 401/403/429 rate. Expected OAuth challenges, expired/revoked credentials and negative tests can contribute; this is not a count of unique callers.

panels.title: Transcript quota and I/O refusals
panels.description: Quota/file-count refusal is distinct from backing disk exhaustion. I/O failures also include lock contention and permissions. No evidence identity or raw error text enters telemetry.

panels.title: Worker snapshot age and computed alert budget
panels.description: Two missed five-minute ticks plus the last measured runtime, minimum 60 seconds; missing duration falls back to 900 seconds. The alert adds a one-minute hold. Read these replacement snapshots directly, never as rates.

panels.title: Managed and gateway-loaded certificate lifetime
panels.description: Managed leaf expiry comes from cert-manager; loaded leaf expiry comes from Traefik. Their agreement is not a network TLS probe or a root/intermediate expiry check. Negative and renewal rehearsals validate every canonical SNI name separately.

panels.title: VM backing filesystem available
panels.description: The spool is a hostPath on VM storage shared with other data. PV declared size is not a hard quota. Labels identify real node filesystems; do not sum duplicate bind mounts. Low byte or inode availability can prevent durable appends.

panels.title: HTTPS edge response rate
panels.description: Canonical auth, login and Recall share this entrypoint. Gateway errors can reveal upstream Ory failures even when Recall application counters are quiet.

panels.title: Remote monitoring target availability
panels.description: Zero means a discovered target is down. Completely missing jobs produce no line and have separate absence alerts. These endpoints are private and grant no access to application Secrets.

panels.title: Fixed dependency reachability
panels.description: One means the fixed tokenless endpoint check passed; zero means it failed. Issuer checks validate canonical HTTPS discovery and public JWKS. Embedding checks expect the protected listener to refuse an anonymous request; this is not inference or credential proof. Missing and stale observations alert separately.

panels.title: Dependency probe completion age
panels.description: Seconds since each fixed probe completed, including failed checks. The once-per-minute CronJob publishes fresh failures. More than 180seconds or a timestamp over 30seconds in the future has a separate alert; an old success does not establish current availability.
